NEW and the reason the 2x2 solve closed at all.  With M_{rho,nu} = <p_rho, h_nu>: (a) M_{rho,nu} = 0 whenever ell(nu) > ell(rho), because the ordered-set-partition count of lem-ph-counting -- stated there for GENERAL rho, not only two-part -- needs ell(nu) nonempty blocks drawn from ell(rho) indices; so M is lower block-triangular for the length filtration, with non-negative integer entries.  (b) M is the Gram matrix of two bases of Lambda^n under a nondegenerate form, hence invertible; in the length order M = [[M^(L),0],[*,D]], so det M = det M^(L) det D != 0 and every leading block M^(L) is invertible.  (c) Hence (Y^lambda_rho)_{ell(rho)<=L} = M^(L) (c_{lambda,nu})_{ell(nu)<=L} for every lambda, through one matrix mentioning neither lambda nor t.  CONSEQUENCE: thm-B is not a two-part accident -- it is exactly the L=2 rows of this, and the composition corollary is the 2x2 back-substitution.  Corroboration: det M^(2) = 2 for n even, 1 for n odd (n=2..8: 2,1,2,1,2,1,2), the 2 coming from the single diagonal entry 1+[x=y], which exists iff n is even.  Verified: (a),(b) for n<=8, every leading determinant nonzero; (c) by recovering c from Y through (M^(L))^{-1} against a direct h-expansion solve for EVERY lambda |- n and every L, n<=7, 0 mismatches (filtration.py).
